gap: No result ChatGPT got states that one Sun Gold Power SG48100P 51.2 V 100 Ah server-rack battery is rated for only 100 A continuous discharge and 100 A continuous charge. A 6.5 kW 48 V split-phase inverter (SPH6548P) draws about 127 A at full output and can charge at up to 140 A, so with a single battery the battery's protection cuts in under heavy load or fast charging. The set needs two batteries in parallel, plus a bus bar and a DC breaker.
standout_why: I compared against ChatGPT's own answer, which says only that separate battery and inverter systems 'require careful electrical design and compatible equipment' and gives no current figures. I also opened the EcoFlow DELTA Pro Ultra US page (result 16), which covers 7.2 kW per unit, Smart Home Panel 2 and installer commissioning but nothing about battery-to-inverter current limits. The Tesla Powerwall pages and datasheets (results 1–15 and 17) cover one unit with the inverter built in, so this mismatch can't happen there. I didn't open those pages one by one; I judged from their titles and the products they describe. None of the results says how many 48 V batteries an inverter of a given size needs. The finding decides the set: the cart needs the SG48100P 2-pack, not one battery. Sun Gold Power's own entry kit (SGM-655M) ships the 6,500 W inverter with only one 100 Ah battery and a 160 A breaker, which makes the trap easy to fall into.
kit_items: Inverter: Sun Gold Power SPH6548P 6.5 kW 48 V split-phase (120/240 V) inverter. Up to 140 A battery charging, UL 1741 by ETL, sold in an approved store (awin:sungoldpower).

Battery: Sun Gold Power SG48100P 2-pack, 2 × 51.2 V 100 Ah (10.24 kWh). Two in parallel allow 200 A continuous discharge and charge, which covers the inverter's ~127 A full-load draw and its 140 A maximum charge. One battery (100 A) does not.
Bus bar: Sun Gold Power 250 A Bus Bar with Cover, 48 VDC (1 pair). Joins the two batteries before the inverter. Sun Gold's own two-battery 6.5 kW kit (SGM-6510M) includes a 250 A bus bar.
DC breaker: Sun Gold Power 160 A DC Breaker between the bus bar and the inverter. This is the size Sun Gold puts in its own 6.5 kW kits.
Not in the cart: a transfer switch or interlock, battery-to-bus-bar cables (Sun Gold's two-battery kit uses 1/0 AWG), and a licensed electrician for the connection to the home panel.
